units.Susanna 1:6: And judicial cases from other cities came to them.
units.Susanna 1:7–8: These men saw a woman lovely in appearance, the wife of their brother from the sons of Israel, named Susanna, daughter of Hilkiah and wife of Joachim, walking in her husband’s garden in the evening. They desired her
units.Susanna 1:9: and distorted their minds, turning their eyes aside so as not to look toward heaven or remember righteous judgments.
units.Susanna 1:10–11: Both were stricken with desire for her, but neither admitted to the other the evil that possessed them concerning her. The woman herself knew nothing of this matter.
units.Susanna 1:12: As dawn came, they would come, trying to outwit one another in their hurry to see who would appear to her first and speak with her.
units.Susanna 1:13–14: And behold, she was walking as usual. One of the elders had arrived, and behold, the other came. One questioned the other, saying, “Why did you go out so early without taking me?” Then each confessed his anguish to the other.
units.Susanna 1:19: One said to the other, “Let us go to her.” Having agreed, they approached her and tried to force her.
units.Susanna 1:22: The Jewish woman said to them, “I know that if I do this, it means death for me; and if I do not, I will not escape your hands.
units.Susanna 1:23: But it is better for me to fall into your hands without having done it than to sin before the Lord.”
units.Susanna 1:28: The lawless men went back, making threats among themselves and plotting to kill her. They came to the assembly of the city where they were residing, and all the sons of Israel who were there sat together in council.
units.Susanna 1:29: The two elders and judges stood up and said, “Send for Susanna, daughter of Hilkiah, who is Joachim’s wife.” They summoned her at once.
units.Susanna 1:30: The woman arrived with her father and mother. Her male and female servants, numbering five hundred, also arrived, together with Susanna’s four children.
units.Susanna 1:32: The lawless men ordered her to be uncovered, so that they might satisfy their desire for her beauty.
units.Susanna 1:33: All her people, and everyone who knew her, wept.
units.Susanna 1:34: The elders and judges stood up and laid their hands on her head.
units.Susanna 1:35: But her heart trusted in the Lord her God. Raising her head, she wept within herself, saying,
units.Susanna 1:35a: “Lord, everlasting God, who knowest all things before they come into being, Thou knowest that I have not done what these lawless men wickedly allege against me.” And the Lord heard her petition.
units.Susanna 1:36: The two elders said, “We were walking in her husband’s garden,
units.Susanna 1:37: and as we went around the course, we saw this woman reclining with a man. We stood and watched them being intimate with one another,
units.Susanna 1:38: and they did not know that we were standing there. Then we said to one another, ‘Let us find out who these people are.’
units.Susanna 1:39: We approached and recognized her, but the young man fled, covered up.
units.Susanna 1:40: We seized her and asked her, ‘Who is the man?’
units.Susanna 1:41: She did not tell us who he was. We testify to these things.” The whole assembly believed them because they were elders and judges of the people.
units.Susanna 1:44–45: And behold, an angel of the Lord was there as she was being led out to perish. As he had been commanded, the angel gave a spirit of understanding to Daniel, who was young.
units.Susanna 1:48: Daniel parted the crowd, stood in their midst, and said, “Are you so foolish, sons of Israel? Have you condemned a daughter of Israel without an inquiry or a clear knowledge of the facts?
units.Susanna 1:51: Now separate them far from one another for me, so that I may examine them.”
units.Susanna 1:52: When they had been separated, Daniel said to the assembly, “Do not now look at the fact that these men are elders and say, ‘They certainly will not lie.’ I will question them according to what occurs to me.” He called one of them, and they brought the elder to the young man. Daniel said to him, “Listen, listen, you who have grown old in evil days! Now your sins have come upon you, the things you formerly did
units.Susanna 1:53: when you were entrusted with hearing and judging cases that bring death: you condemned the innocent and would release the guilty, although the Lord says, ‘You shall not kill the innocent and the righteous.’
units.Susanna 1:54: Now then, under what tree, and in what part of the garden, did you see them together?” The impious man said, “Under a mastic tree.”
units.Susanna 1:55: The young man said, “You have indeed lied against your own soul, for the angel of the Lord will split your soul today.”
units.Susanna 1:56: He moved this man aside and said to bring the other to him. To this man he said, “Why is your offspring corrupted, like Sidon’s and not like Judah’s? Beauty and filthy desire deceived you!
units.Susanna 1:57: This is how you used to treat the daughters of Israel, and they were intimate with you because they were afraid. But a daughter of Judah did not endure bearing your disease in lawlessness.
units.Susanna 1:58: Now then, tell me: under what tree, and in what part of the garden, did you catch them being intimate with one another?” He said, “Under a holm-oak.”
units.Susanna 1:59: Daniel said, “Sinner, the angel of the Lord now stands holding his sword, until the people utterly destroy you both, so that he may saw you apart.”
units.Susanna 1:60–62: The whole assembly cried out over the young man, because from their own mouths he had established that both were admittedly false witnesses. As the law prescribes, they did to them what they had wickedly plotted against their sister. They gagged them, took them out, and threw them into a ravine. Then the angel of the Lord cast fire through their midst. Innocent blood was saved that day.
units.Susanna 1:63: For this reason the young are beloved of Jacob in their simplicity. Let us also be attentive to capable young sons, for the young will be devout, and a spirit of knowledge and understanding will be in them for ever and ever.
units.Bel and Dragon 1:1: From the prophecy of Habakkuk, son of Joshua, of the tribe of Levi.
units.Bel and Dragon 1:2: There was a certain priest named Daniel, son of Abal, a companion of the king of Babylon.
units.Bel and Dragon 1:3: There was an idol, Bel, whom the Babylonians revered. Each day twelve artabas of fine flour, four sheep, and six metretas of oil were expended for him.
units.Bel and Dragon 1:4: The king revered him and went each day to bow before him, but Daniel prayed to the Lord.
units.Bel and Dragon 1:5: The king said to Daniel, “Why do you not bow before Bel?” Daniel said to the king, “I revere no one except the Lord God, who created heaven and earth and has lordship over all flesh.”
units.Bel and Dragon 1:6: The king said to him, “Is this one, then, not a god? Do you not see how much is spent on him every day?”
units.Bel and Dragon 1:7: Daniel said to him, “Certainly not! Let no one deceive you. This one is clay on the inside and bronze on the outside. I swear to you by the Lord, the God of gods, that this one has never eaten anything.”
units.Bel and Dragon 1:8: The king became angry, called those in charge of the temple, and said to them, “Show who eats what is prepared for Bel. Otherwise, either you will die or Daniel, who claims that these things are not eaten by him.” They said, “Bel himself is the one who eats them.”
units.Bel and Dragon 1:9: Daniel said to the king, “Let it be so. If I do not demonstrate that Bel is not the one who eats these things, I and all my people will die.” Bel had seventy priests, apart from their wives and children.
units.Bel and Dragon 1:10: They brought the king into the idol-temple.
units.Bel and Dragon 1:11: The food was set out before the king and Daniel. Mixed wine was brought in and placed before Bel. Daniel said, “You yourself see that these things are laid out, O king. So seal the locks of the temple yourself when it has been closed.”
units.Bel and Dragon 1:14: Daniel ordered his people to put everyone out of the temple and sprinkle the whole temple with ashes, without anyone outside his own group knowing. Then he ordered the temple to be sealed with the king’s ring and the rings of certain distinguished priests. It was done that way.
units.Bel and Dragon 1:15–17: The next day they came to the place. Meanwhile, Bel’s priests had entered through secret doors, eaten everything laid before Bel, and drunk all the wine. Daniel said, “Men who are priests, inspect your seals to see whether they remain. And you, O king, examine whether anything has turned out contrary to what you expected.” They found the seal as it had been, and removed the seal.
units.Bel and Dragon 1:18: They opened the doors and saw that everything set out had been consumed and the tables were empty. The king rejoiced and said to Daniel, “Bel is great, and there is no deceit in him.”
units.Bel and Dragon 1:19: Daniel laughed heartily and said to the king, “Come, see the priests’ deceit.” Daniel said, “O king, whose footprints are these?”
units.Bel and Dragon 1:20: The king said, “Those of men, women, and children.”
units.Bel and Dragon 1:21: He went to the house where the priests were staying and found Bel’s food and the wine. Daniel showed the king the secret doors through which the priests would enter and consume what was laid before Bel.
units.Bel and Dragon 1:22: The king brought them out of Bel’s temple and handed them over to Daniel. He gave Daniel the expenditure allocated to Bel, and destroyed Bel.
units.Bel and Dragon 1:23: There was a dragon in the same place, and the Babylonians revered it.
units.Bel and Dragon 1:24: The king said to Daniel, “Will you say that this one is bronze too? Behold, it lives, eats, and drinks. Bow before it.”
units.Bel and Dragon 1:25: Daniel said, “O king, give me authority, and I will kill the dragon without iron or a rod.”
units.Bel and Dragon 1:26: The king consented and said to him, “It is granted to you.”
units.Bel and Dragon 1:27: Daniel took thirty minas of pitch, together with fat and hair, boiled them together, made a cake, and threw it into the dragon’s mouth. It ate and burst apart. He showed it to the king, saying, “Are these not the things you revere, O king?”
units.Bel and Dragon 1:28: All the people from the country gathered against Daniel and said, “The king has become a Jew! He has destroyed Bel and killed the dragon.”
units.Bel and Dragon 1:30: The king saw that the crowd of the country had gathered against him. He called his companions and said, “I hand Daniel over to destruction.”
units.Bel and Dragon 1:31–32: There was a pit in which seven lions were kept. Those who plotted against the king were handed over to them, and each day two bodies of people condemned to death were supplied to them. The crowds threw Daniel into that pit so that he would be devoured and would not even receive burial. Daniel was in the pit for six days.
units.Bel and Dragon 1:33: On the sixth day, Habakkuk had bread crumbled in a trough with stew, and a jar of mixed wine. He was going into the field to the reapers.
units.Bel and Dragon 1:34: An angel of the Lord spoke to Habakkuk, saying, “Thus says the Lord God to you: ‘Take the meal you have to Daniel in the lions’ pit in Babylon.’”
units.Bel and Dragon 1:35: Habakkuk said, “Lord God, I have not seen Babylon, and I do not know where the pit is.”
units.Bel and Dragon 1:36: The angel of the Lord took Habakkuk by the hair of his head and set him above the pit in Babylon.
units.Bel and Dragon 1:37: Habakkuk said to Daniel, “Get up and eat the meal that the Lord God has sent you.”
units.Bel and Dragon 1:38: Daniel said, “For the Lord God has remembered me, He who does not abandon those who love Him.”
units.Bel and Dragon 1:39: Daniel ate. The angel of the Lord returned Habakkuk to the place from which he had taken him on that same day. And the Lord God remembered Daniel.
units.Bel and Dragon 1:40: After these things the king went out mourning Daniel. He bent down into the pit and saw him sitting there.
units.Bel and Dragon 1:41: The king cried aloud and said, “The Lord God is great, and there is no other besides Him.”
units.Bel and Dragon 1:42: The king brought Daniel out of the pit. Before Daniel’s eyes he threw into the pit those responsible for his destruction, and they were devoured.
units.Matthew 5:27: You have heard that it was said: ‘You shall not commit adultery.’
units.Matthew 5:28: But I tell you that everyone who looks at a woman to lust after her has already committed adultery with her in his heart.
units.Matthew 5:29: If your right eye causes you to stumble, pluck it out and throw it away from you; for it is better for you that one of your members perish than that your whole body be thrown into Gehenna.
units.Matthew 5:30: And if your right hand causes you to stumble, cut it off and throw it away from you; for it is better for you that one of your members perish than that your whole body go into Gehenna.
units.Proverbs 6:20: Son, guard your father’s laws, and do not reject your mother’s ordinances.
units.Proverbs 6:21: Fasten them always upon your soul, and collar them around your neck.
units.Proverbs 6:22: Whenever you walk, take her along and let her be with you; when you sleep, let her guard you, so that when you rise she may converse with you,
units.Proverbs 6:23: because the commandment of law is a lamp and a light, and correction and discipline are life’s way,
units.Proverbs 6:24: to preserve you from a married woman and from an alien tongue’s slander.
units.Proverbs 6:25: Do not let desire for beauty overcome you; do not be hunted by your own eyes, nor seized by her eyelids.
units.Proverbs 6:26: For a prostitute’s price is as much as one loaf, but a woman hunts men’s precious lives.
units.Proverbs 6:27: Will someone bind fire in his bosom without burning his garments?
units.Proverbs 6:28: Or will someone walk on fiery coals without burning his feet?
units.Proverbs 6:29: So is the one who goes in to a married woman: he will not be acquitted, nor will anyone touching her.
units.Proverbs 6:30: It is no wonder if someone is caught stealing, for he steals to fill his appetite when hungry.
units.Proverbs 6:31: But if caught, he will repay sevenfold, and by giving all his possessions he will rescue himself.
units.Proverbs 6:32: But the adulterer, through lack of sense, brings destruction upon his own life;
units.Proverbs 6:33: he bears pains and dishonors, and his reproach will never be wiped away.
units.Proverbs 6:34: For her husband’s anger is full of jealousy; he will not spare on the day of judgment,
units.Proverbs 6:35: he will not trade his enmity for any ransom, nor be reconciled by many gifts.
units.Proverbs 1:10: Son, do not let ungodly men lead you astray; do not agree if they invite you, saying,
units.Proverbs 1:11: Come with us; share in bloodshed. Let us hide a righteous man in the earth unjustly;
units.Proverbs 1:12: let us swallow him alive like Hades and remove his memory from the earth.
units.Proverbs 1:13: Let us seize his costly property and fill our houses with spoils.
units.Proverbs 1:14: Cast your lot among us; let us all obtain a common purse, and let there be one moneybag for us.
units.Proverbs 1:15: Do not walk in the way with them; turn your foot away from their paths,
units.Proverbs 1:16: for their feet run toward evil, and they are quick to shed blood.
units.Proverbs 1:17: For nets are not unjustly stretched out for winged creatures.
units.Proverbs 1:18: For those who share in murder store up evils for themselves, and the overthrow of lawless men is evil.
units.Proverbs 1:19: These are the ways of all who carry out lawless deeds, for through ungodliness they take away their own life.
units.Genesis 39:1: And Joseph was brought down into Egypt; and Potiphar, Pharaoh’s eunuch, the chief cook, an Egyptian man, bought him from the hands of the Ishmaelites who had brought him down there.
units.Genesis 39:2: And the Lord was with Joseph, and he was a prosperous man; and he was in the house of his Egyptian master.
units.Genesis 39:3: And his master knew that the Lord was with him, and that whatever he did, the Lord made it prosper in his hands.
units.Genesis 39:4: And Joseph found grace before his master, and pleased him; and he set him over his house, and committed all that he had into Joseph’s hand.
units.Genesis 39:5: And after he was set over his house and over all that he had, the Lord blessed the Egyptian’s house for Joseph’s sake; and the blessing of the Lord was upon all that he had, in the house and in the field.
units.Genesis 39:6: And he committed all that he had into Joseph’s hands, and concerned himself with nothing except the bread which he ate. And Joseph was handsome in form, and very beautiful to look at.
units.Genesis 39:7: And after these things his master’s wife cast her eyes upon Joseph, and said, “Lie with me.”
units.Genesis 39:8: But he would not, and said to his master’s wife, “If my master concerns himself with nothing in his house because of me, and has committed all that he has into my hands,
units.Genesis 39:9: “and nothing in this house is above me, and nothing has been withheld from me except you, because you are his wife, how shall I do this evil thing, and sin before God?”
units.Genesis 39:10: And though she spoke to Joseph day after day, he did not listen to her, to sleep with her and have relations with her.
units.Genesis 39:11: And on a certain day Joseph entered the house to do his work, and none of the household was inside.
units.Genesis 39:12: And she caught him by his garments, saying, “Lie with me.” And he left his garments in her hands, and fled and went outside.
units.Genesis 39:13: And when she saw that he had left his garments in her hands, and had fled and gone outside,
units.Genesis 39:14: she called those of the household, and said to them, “See, he has brought us a Hebrew servant to mock us. He came in to me, saying, ‘Lie with me’; and I cried with a loud voice.
units.Genesis 39:15: “And when he heard that I lifted up my voice and cried, he left his garments beside me, and fled and went outside.”
units.Genesis 39:16: And she kept his garments beside her until his master came to his house.
units.Genesis 39:17: And she spoke to him in this way, saying, “The Hebrew servant whom you have brought to us came in to me to mock me, and said to me, ‘I will lie with you.’
units.Genesis 39:18: “And when he heard that I lifted up my voice and cried, he left his garments beside me, and fled and went outside.”
units.Genesis 39:19: And when his master heard the words of his wife which she spoke to him, saying, “This is what your servant did to me,” his anger was kindled.
units.Genesis 39:20: And Joseph’s master took him and cast him into the fortress, into the place where the king’s prisoners were held in the fortress.
units.Genesis 39:21: And the Lord was with Joseph, and poured mercy upon him, and gave him grace before the chief jailer.
units.Genesis 39:22: And the chief jailer committed the prison into Joseph’s hand, and all those confined in the prison, and all that they did there.
units.Genesis 39:23: And the chief jailer concerned himself with nothing because of him; for all was in Joseph’s hand, because the Lord was with him, and whatever he did, the Lord made it prosper in his hands.
units.Psalms 36:12: The sinner will watch the righteous closely and gnash his teeth at him.
units.Psalms 36:13: But the Lord will laugh him to scorn, for He foresees that his day will come.
units.Psalms 36:14: The sinners drew a sword and stretched their bow, to cast down the poor and needy, to slaughter the upright in heart.
units.Psalms 36:15: May their sword enter their own heart, and may their bows be shattered.
units.Leviticus 24:10: And the son of an Israelite woman, whose father was an Egyptian man, went out among the sons of Israel. The Israelite woman’s son and an Israelite man fought in the camp.
units.Leviticus 24:11: And the Israelite woman’s son pronounced the Name and cursed, and they brought him unto Moses. His mother’s name was Shelomith daughter of Dibri, of the tribe of Dan.
units.Leviticus 24:12: And they placed him in custody, to judge him by the Lord’s command.
units.Leviticus 24:13: And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
units.Leviticus 24:14: Bring the one who cursed outside the camp. All who heard him shall lay their hands on his head, and the whole congregation shall stone him.
units.Leviticus 24:15: And speak unto the sons of Israel, and you shall say unto them: A man who curses God shall bear sin.
units.Leviticus 24:16: Let one who names the Lord’s name surely be put to death. Let the whole congregation of Israel stone him with stones. Whether resident foreigner or native-born, when he names the Lord’s name, let him die.
units.Psalms 55:1: For the end. Concerning the people far removed from the holy ones. Of David, for an inscription on a pillar, when the foreigners seized him in Gath.
units.Psalms 55:2: Have mercy on me, Lord, for a man trampled me; fighting all day, he afflicted me.
units.Psalms 55:3: My enemies trampled me all day, for many are those fighting me from a height.
units.Psalms 55:4: By day I will fear, but I will hope in Thee.
units.Psalms 55:5: In God I will praise my words all day. In God I have hoped; I will not fear. What will flesh do to me?
units.Psalms 55:6: All day they detested my words; all their thoughts against me are for evil.
units.Sirach 23:18: A man who transgresses from his marriage bed says in his soul, “Who sees me? Darkness is around me, and the walls cover me; no one sees me. What should I fear? The Most High will certainly not remember my sins.”
units.Sirach 23:19: Human eyes are what he fears; he does not know that the Lord’s eyes are ten thousand times brighter than the sun, surveying every human way and observing hidden places.
units.Sirach 23:20: Before all things were created, they were known to Him, and likewise after they were completed.
units.Sirach 23:21: This man will receive retribution in the city’s squares and be seized where he did not suspect it.
units.Romans 1:21: because, although they knew God, they did not glorify Him as God or give thanks, but became futile in their thoughts, and their senseless heart was darkened.
units.Romans 1:22: Claiming to be wise, they became foolish,
units.Romans 1:23: and exchanged the glory of the incorruptible God for the likeness of an image of corruptible humanity, and of birds and four-footed animals and creeping things.
units.Romans 1:24: Therefore God handed them over, in the desires of their hearts, to impurity, so that their bodies would be dishonored among them,
units.Romans 1:25: who exchanged the truth of God for the lie, and revered and worshiped the creation instead of the Creator, who is blessed throughout the ages. Amen.
units.Romans 1:26: For this reason God handed them over to dishonorable passions; for their females exchanged natural relations for those contrary to nature,
units.Romans 1:27: and likewise the males, leaving natural relations with the female, burned in their desire for one another, males with males committing what is shameful and receiving in themselves the due penalty for their error.
units.Romans 1:28: And just as they did not see fit to retain God in their knowledge, God handed them over to an unfit mind, to do what is not fitting:
units.Romans 1:29: filled with all unrighteousness, wickedness, greed, evil; full of envy, murder, strife, deceit, malice; whisperers,
units.Romans 1:30: slanderers, haters of God, insolent, proud, boastful, inventors of evils, disobedient to parents,
units.Romans 1:31: without understanding, faithless, without natural affection, merciless;
units.Romans 1:32: who, knowing God’s righteous decree, that those who practice such things are worthy of death, not only do them, but also approve those who practice them.
units.Luke 23:25: He released the man who had been thrown into prison for uprising and murder, whom they were demanding; but he handed Jesus over to their will.
units.Luke 23:26: As they led Him away, they seized a certain Simon of Cyrene coming from the countryside, and laid the cross on him to carry behind Jesus.
units.Luke 23:27: And a great multitude of the people followed Him, and women who beat themselves in mourning and lamented Him.
units.Luke 23:28: But Jesus turned toward them and said, “Daughters of Jerusalem, do not weep over Me, but weep over yourselves and over your children.
units.Luke 23:29: For behold, days are coming in which they will say, ‘Blessed are the barren, and the wombs that did not bear, and the breasts that did not nourish.’
units.Luke 23:30: Then they will begin to say to the mountains, ‘Fall upon us,’ and to the hills, ‘Cover us.’
units.Luke 23:31: For if they do these things with the green wood, what will happen with the dry?”
units.Daniel 1:1: In the third year of King Joakim of Judea, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon arrived at Jerusalem and besieged it.
units.Daniel 1:2: The Lord handed the city into his hands, together with Joakim king of Judea and a portion of the Lord’s sacred vessels. He carried them away to Babylon and deposited them in his idol-temple.
units.Daniel 1:3: The king told Abiesdri, his chief eunuch, to bring him some of the sons of Israel’s magnates, of the royal family and of the chosen men:
units.Daniel 1:4: young men without blemish, handsome, knowledgeable in every kind of wisdom, literate, intelligent, wise, and strong enough to be in the king’s house, and to teach them letters and the Chaldean tongue,
units.Daniel 1:5: and to give them a ration from the king’s house each day, from the royal table and the wine the king drank, and to educate them for three years and place some of them before the king.
units.Daniel 1:6: Among the lineage of Israel’s sons from Judea were Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah.
units.Daniel 1:7: The chief eunuch assigned them names: Daniel, Baltasar; Hananiah, Sedrach; Mishael, Misach; and Azariah, Abdenago.
units.Daniel 1:8: Daniel considered in his heart how he might avoid being polluted by the king’s dinner and the wine he drank, and petitioned the chief eunuch that he might not be contaminated.
units.Daniel 1:9: The Lord gave Daniel honor and favor before the chief eunuch.
units.Daniel 1:10: The chief eunuch said to Daniel, “I am anxious about my lord the king, who prescribed your food and drink, lest he see your faces drawn and weak beside the foreign youths being reared with you, and I risk my own neck.”
units.Daniel 1:11: Daniel said to Abiesdri, appointed chief eunuch over Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah,
units.Daniel 1:12: “Test your servants for ten days, and let us be given legumes from the earth to eat, and water to drink.
units.Daniel 1:13: If our appearance looks drawn beside the other young men eating the royal dinner, then deal with your servants however you wish.”
units.Daniel 1:14: He dealt with them in this manner and tested them for ten days.
units.Daniel 1:15: After ten days their appearance was good and their bodily condition better than the other young men eating the royal dinner.
units.Daniel 1:16: Abiesdri kept removing their dinner and wine and giving them legumes in exchange.
units.Daniel 1:17: The Lord gave the young men knowledge, understanding, and practical wisdom in every literary skill; to Daniel He gave understanding in every utterance, vision, dreams, and all wisdom.
units.Daniel 1:18: After these days the king ordered them brought in, and the chief eunuch brought them before King Nebuchadnezzar.
units.Daniel 1:19: The king conversed with them, and among the wise no one was found like Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah. They remained beside the king.
units.Daniel 1:20: In every matter of discourse, understanding, and education about which the king questioned them, he found them ten times wiser than the learned experts and philosophers throughout his kingdom. The king honored them, appointed them rulers, and declared them wiser than all his own men in affairs throughout his land and kingdom.
units.Daniel 1:21: Daniel remained until the first year of the reign of Cyrus king of the Persians.
units.John 7:45: So the officers came to the chief priests and Pharisees, and these said to them, “Why did you not bring Him?”
units.John 7:46: The officers answered, “Never has a person spoken in this way.”
units.John 7:47: So the Pharisees answered them, “Have you also been led astray?
units.John 7:48: Has any of the rulers believed in Him, or any of the Pharisees?
units.John 7:49: But this crowd that does not know the Law is accursed.”
units.John 7:50: Nicodemus, who had come to Him earlier and was one of them, said to them,
units.John 7:51: “Does our Law judge a person unless it first hears from him and knows what he does?”
units.John 7:52: They answered him, “Are you also from Galilee? Search and see that a prophet does not arise from Galilee.”
units.Deuteronomy 19:15: One witness shall not suffice to testify against a man concerning any injustice, or any trespass, or any sin which he sins. At the mouth of two witnesses, and at the mouth of three witnesses, shall every matter be established.
units.Deuteronomy 19:16: And if an unrighteous witness rises up against a man, accusing him of ungodliness,
units.Deuteronomy 19:17: then the two men between whom is the dispute shall stand before the Lord, and before the priests, and before the judges who shall be in those days.
units.Deuteronomy 19:18: And the judges shall inquire diligently; and behold, if the unrighteous witness has testified falsely, and has stood against his brother,
units.Deuteronomy 19:19: then you shall do unto him as he wickedly purposed to do unto his brother; and you shall remove the evil one from among yourselves.
units.Deuteronomy 19:20: And those who remain shall hear and fear, and shall no more do such an evil thing among you.
units.Deuteronomy 19:21: Your eye shall not spare him: life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot.
units.Exodus 23:1: “You shall not receive an empty report. You shall not agree with the unrighteous to become an unrighteous witness.
units.Exodus 23:2: You shall not join the many in evil; neither shall you join a multitude in turning aside with the many, to turn aside judgment.
units.Exodus 23:3: Neither shall you favour a poor man in judgment.
units.Exodus 23:4: And if you meet your enemy’s ox or his beast of burden wandering, you shall surely turn it back and restore it to him.
units.Exodus 23:5: And if you see your enemy’s beast of burden fallen beneath its load, you shall not pass it by; but you shall raise it up together with him.
units.Exodus 23:6: You shall not pervert the judgment of a poor man in his cause.
units.Exodus 23:7: You shall keep far away from every unrighteous charge; the innocent and the righteous you shall not kill, neither shall you justify the ungodly for gifts.
units.Exodus 23:8: And you shall receive no gifts; for gifts blind the eyes of those who see, and corrupt righteous words.
units.Exodus 23:9: And you shall not afflict a resident foreigner; for you know the soul of the resident foreigner, since you yourselves were resident foreigners in the land of Egypt.
units.Proverbs 19:5: A false witness will not be unpunished, and one who accuses unjustly will not escape.
units.Proverbs 19:6: Many attend the faces of kings, but every evil person becomes a reproach to a man.
units.Proverbs 19:7: Everyone who hates a poor brother will also be far from friendship. A good thought will draw near to those who know it, and an intelligent man will find it. One who does many evils brings wickedness to completion, and one who provokes words will not be saved.
units.Proverbs 19:8: One who acquires understanding loves himself, and one who keeps understanding will find good things.
units.Proverbs 19:9: A false witness will not be unpunished, and whoever kindles wickedness will perish by it.
units.Numbers 22:21: And Balaam rose in the morning, saddled his donkey, and went with the officials of Moab.
units.Numbers 22:22: And God grew angry because he went. God's angel rose to obstruct him. Balaam was riding his donkey, with his two servants beside him.
units.Numbers 22:23: And the donkey saw God's angel opposing them in the road with his sword drawn in his hand. She turned off the road into the plain, and he struck her with the staff to direct her onto the road.
units.Numbers 22:24: And God's angel stood in the furrows of the vineyards, with a fence on either side.
units.Numbers 22:25: And the donkey saw God's angel and pressed herself against the wall, crushing Balaam's foot. He whipped her again.
units.Numbers 22:26: And God's angel went farther and stood in a narrow place where there was no way to turn right or left.
units.Numbers 22:27: And the donkey saw God's angel and crouched beneath Balaam. Balaam became angry and beat the donkey with his staff.
units.Numbers 22:28: And God opened the donkey's mouth, and she says to Balaam: What have I done unto you that you have struck me this third time?
units.Numbers 22:29: And Balaam said to the donkey: Because you have mocked me! If I had a sword in my hand, I would have stabbed you already.
units.Numbers 22:30: And the donkey says to Balaam: Am I not your donkey, which you have ridden from your youth until this day? Have I acted like this toward you out of deliberate disregard? He said: No.
units.Numbers 22:31: God uncovered Balaam's eyes, and he sees the Lord's angel opposing him in the road with his sword drawn in his hand. He bent down and prostrated himself on his face.
units.Numbers 22:32: And God's angel said to him: Why have you struck your donkey this third time? Behold, I have come out to oppose you, because your way is not fitting before me.
units.Numbers 22:33: And the donkey saw me and turned away from me this third time. If she had not turned away, I would now have killed you and preserved her.
units.Numbers 22:34: And Balaam said unto the Lord's angel: I have sinned, for I did not know that you were opposing me in the road. Now, if this does not please you, I will turn back.
units.Numbers 22:35: And God's angel said to Balaam: Go with the men, but take care to speak the word that I tell you. Balaam went with Balak's officials.
units.Job 32:1: His three friends also ceased contradicting Job any further, for Job was righteous before them.
units.Job 32:2: Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite, of the kindred of Ram in the land of Ausitis, became angry. He was very angry with Job because Job declared himself righteous before the Lord.
units.Job 32:3: He was also very angry with the three friends, because they could not give Job a contrary answer and declared him ungodly.
units.Job 32:4: Elihu waited to give Job an answer, because they were older than he in days.
units.Job 32:5: Elihu saw that there was no answer in the mouth of the three men, and his anger blazed.
units.Job 32:6: Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite replied: “I am younger in time, and you are older; therefore I kept quiet, afraid to announce my own knowledge to you.
units.Job 32:7: I said, ‘Time is what speaks, and in many years people know wisdom.’
units.Job 32:8: But there is a spirit in mortals, and the Almighty’s breath is what teaches.
units.Job 32:9: The long-lived are not wise, nor do elders know judgment.
units.Job 32:10: Therefore I said, ‘Listen to me, and I will announce to you what I know.’
units.Daniel 6:1: Artaxerxes of the Medes received the kingdom. Darius was full of days and glorious in old age.
units.Daniel 6:2: He appointed one hundred twenty-seven satraps over his whole kingdom,
units.Daniel 6:3: and over them three men as their leaders. Daniel was one of the three men,
units.Daniel 6:4: having authority above everyone in the kingdom. Daniel was clothed in purple, great and glorious before King Darius, because he was distinguished, knowledgeable, and understanding, with a holy spirit in him, and prospered in the king’s affairs that he conducted. Then the king decided to appoint Daniel over his whole kingdom, along with the two men whom he had appointed with him and one hundred twenty-seven satraps.
units.Daniel 6:5: When the king decided to appoint Daniel over his whole kingdom, the two young men devised a plan and resolution together. Since they could find no sin or ignorant fault in Daniel of which they could accuse him before the king,
units.Daniel 6:6: they said, “Come, let us establish a restriction binding upon ourselves: no one is to make a request or offer a prayer to any god for thirty days, except to King Darius; otherwise he will die.” They intended to bring Daniel down before the king and have him thrown into the lions’ pit, for they knew that Daniel prayed and entreated the Lord his God three times a day.
units.Daniel 6:7: Then those men approached and said before the king:
units.Daniel 6:8: “We have established a restriction and decree: anyone who offers a prayer or makes any request to any god for thirty days, except to King Darius, will be thrown into the lions’ pit.”
units.Daniel 6:9: They asked the king to establish the restriction and not alter it, because they knew that Daniel prayed and entreated three times a day; they intended him to be brought down through the king and thrown into the lions’ pit.
units.Daniel 6:10: Thus King Darius established and ratified it.
units.Daniel 6:11: When Daniel learned of the restriction established against him, he opened windows in his upper room toward Jerusalem, fell upon his face three times a day as he had done before, and made supplication.
units.Daniel 6:12: They watched Daniel and caught him praying three times a day, every day.
units.Daniel 6:13: Then these men appealed to the king and said, “King Darius, did you not decree a restriction that no one should offer a prayer or make a request to any god for thirty days except to you, O king, otherwise he would be thrown into the lions’ pit?” The king answered them, “The statement is exact, and the restriction will remain.”
units.Daniel 6:13a: They said to him, “We adjure you by the decrees of the Medes and Persians: do not alter the command, show partiality, or diminish anything that has been stated; punish the man who has not kept this restriction.” He said, “I will do as you say; this is established with me.”
units.Daniel 6:14: They said, “Behold! We found Daniel your friend praying and seeking the face of his God three times a day.”
units.Daniel 6:15: The king, grieved, ordered Daniel thrown into the lions’ pit according to the restriction he had established against him. Then the king was deeply grieved over Daniel and tried to rescue him from the satraps’ hands until sunset,
units.Daniel 6:16: but could not rescue him from them.
units.Daniel 6:17: King Darius cried out and said to Daniel, “Your God, whom you worship continually three times a day, will rescue you from the lions’ power. Take courage until morning.”
units.Daniel 6:18: Then Daniel was thrown into the lions’ pit. A stone was brought and placed at the pit’s mouth, and the king sealed it with his own ring and his magnates’ rings, so that Daniel could not be taken away from them, nor could the king pull him up from the pit.
units.Daniel 6:19: Then the king returned to his royal residence and spent the night fasting, grieving over Daniel. Daniel’s God, taking care of him, shut the lions’ mouths, and they did not trouble Daniel.
units.Daniel 6:20: King Darius rose early in the morning, took the satraps with him, and went and stood at the mouth of the lions’ pit.
units.Daniel 6:21: Then the king called to Daniel with a loud voice and weeping: “O Daniel, are you perhaps alive? Has your God, whom you worship continually, saved you from the lions, so that they have not destroyed you?”
units.Daniel 6:22: Then Daniel answered with a loud voice and said, “O king, I am still alive,
units.Daniel 6:23: and God has saved me from the lions, because righteousness was found in me before Him. Before you also, O king, neither ignorant fault nor sin was found in me. Yet you listened to men who mislead kings and threw me into the lions’ pit for destruction.”
units.Daniel 6:24: Then all the forces assembled and saw Daniel, whom the lions had not troubled.
units.Daniel 6:25: Then those two men who had testified against Daniel, with their wives and children, were thrown to the lions. The lions killed them and crushed their bones.
units.Daniel 6:26: Then Darius wrote to all nations, countries, and languages dwelling throughout his whole land, saying:
units.Daniel 6:27: “Let all people in my kingdom bow to and worship Daniel’s God, for He is God who endures and lives from generation to generation for ever.
units.Daniel 6:28: I, Darius, will bow to Him and serve Him all my days, for handmade idols cannot save as Daniel’s God redeemed Daniel.”
units.Daniel 6:29: King Darius was gathered to his people, and Daniel was appointed in Darius’s reign. Cyrus the Persian received his kingdom.
units.Daniel 2:1: In the second year of Nebuchadnezzar’s reign, the king fell into visions and dreams and was disturbed in his dream, and his sleep left him.
units.Daniel 2:2: The king ordered the incantation-singers, magi, and sorcerers of the Chaldeans brought in to report his dreams to him. They arrived and stood beside the king.
units.Daniel 2:3: The king said to them, “I have seen a dream, and my spirit was stirred; therefore I wish to understand the dream.”
units.Daniel 2:4: The Chaldeans spoke to the king in the Syrian language: “My lord king, live for ever! Report your dream to your servants, and we will explain its interpretation to you.”
units.Daniel 2:5: The king answered the Chaldeans, “Unless you truthfully report the dream to me and disclose its interpretation, you will be made a public example, and your possessions will be taken into the royal treasury.
units.Daniel 2:6: But if you make the dream clear to me and report its interpretation, you will receive gifts of every kind and be honored by me. Disclose the dream to me and interpret it.”
units.Nehemiah 9:5: The Levites Jesus and Kadmiel said, “Stand up and bless the Lord your God from everlasting to everlasting. They will bless Thy glorious name and exalt it above all blessing and praise.”
units.Nehemiah 9:6: Esdras said, “Thou alone art the Lord. Thou madest heaven, the heaven of heaven and all their array, the earth and everything in it, the seas and everything in them. Thou givest life to all things, and the armies of heaven worship Thee.
units.Nehemiah 9:7: “Thou art the Lord God. Thou didst choose Abram, bring him out of the country of the Chaldeans and give him the name Abraam.
units.Nehemiah 9:8: “Thou didst find his heart faithful before Thee and make a covenant with him to give him the land of the Chananites, Chettites, Amorrites, Pherezites, Jebousites and Gergesites, and to his offspring. Thou didst fulfil Thy words, for Thou art righteous.
units.Psalms 49:7: “Hear, My people, and I will speak unto you; Israel, I testify unto you. I am God, your God.
units.Psalms 49:8: I will not rebuke you concerning your sacrifices; your burnt offerings are continually before Me.
units.Psalms 49:9: I will not receive calves from your house or young goats from your flocks.
units.Psalms 49:10: For all the forest’s wild animals are Mine, beasts on the mountains and cattle.
units.Psalms 49:11: I know all the birds of heaven, and the field’s beauty is with Me.
units.Psalms 49:12: If I become hungry, I will certainly not tell you, for the inhabited world and its fullness are Mine.
units.Psalms 49:13: Will I eat bulls’ flesh or drink goats’ blood?
units.Psalms 49:14: Sacrifice a sacrifice of praise to God and pay your vows to the Most High.
units.Psalms 49:15: Call on Me in the day of affliction; I will rescue you, and you will glorify Me.” Diapsalma.
units.Psalms 113:12: The idols of the nations are silver and gold, works of human hands.
units.Psalms 113:13: They have a mouth and will not speak; they have eyes and will not see.
units.Psalms 113:14: They have ears and will not hear; they have noses and will not smell.
units.Psalms 113:15: They have hands and will not feel; feet, and will not walk; they will not sound with their throat.
units.Psalms 113:16: May those who make them become like them, and all who have put their trust in them.
units.Psalms 113:17: The house of Israel hoped in the Lord; He is their helper and their defender.
units.Psalms 113:18: The house of Aaron hoped in the Lord; He is their helper and their defender.
units.Psalms 113:19: Those who fear the Lord hoped in the Lord; He is their helper and their defender.
units.Jeremiah 27:1: The Lord’s word that He spoke against Babylon:
units.Jeremiah 27:2: Announce among the nations and make it heard; do not hide it. Say, Babylon has been captured! Bel was disgraced, the fearless one; the delicate one was handed over, Marodach.
units.Jeremiah 27:3: A nation came up against her from the north; it will make her land a ruin, with no one living in it, from human to livestock.
units.Habakkuk 1:1: The oracle that Habakkuk the prophet saw.
units.Habakkuk 1:2: How long, Lord, shall I cry and Thou wilt not listen? I shall cry to Thee while being wronged, and Thou wilt not save?
units.Habakkuk 1:3: Why didst Thou show me toil and pain, to look upon misery and impiety? Judgment has come against me, and the judge takes.
units.Habakkuk 1:4: Therefore law has been scattered, and judgment is not brought to completion; the impious oppresses the righteous, so judgment will go forth distorted.
units.Habakkuk 2:18: What use is a carved image, that they carved it? They formed it as a cast object, a false appearance, because its maker trusted his creation, making mute idols.
units.Habakkuk 2:19: Woe to the one saying to wood, ‘Wake and rise!’ and to stone, ‘Be lifted up!’ It is an appearance, a plate of gold and silver, and no breath at all is in it.
units.Habakkuk 2:20: But the Lord is in His holy sanctuary; let all the earth revere Him.”
units.Luke 23:13: Pilate called together the chief priests, the rulers, and the people
units.Luke 23:14: and said to them, “You brought this man to me as one turning the people astray. And behold, I examined Him before you and found no ground in this man for the accusations you bring against Him.
units.Luke 23:15: Nor did Herod, for he sent Him back to us. And behold, nothing deserving death has been done by Him.
units.Luke 23:16: Therefore I will punish Him and release Him.”
units.Luke 23:18: But they cried out all together, saying, “Take this man away, and release Barabbas to us!”
units.Luke 23:19: He had been thrown into prison for a certain uprising that took place in the city and for murder.
units.Luke 23:20: Pilate addressed them again, wanting to release Jesus.
units.Luke 23:21: But they kept shouting, saying, “Crucify, crucify Him!”
units.Luke 23:22: And for the third time he said to them, “Why, what evil has this man done? I found no ground for death in Him. Therefore I will punish Him and release Him.”
units.Luke 23:23: But they pressed him with loud voices, demanding that He be crucified, and their voices prevailed.
units.Luke 23:24: And Pilate decided that their demand should be granted.
units.Acts 19:23: About that time a serious disturbance arose concerning the Way.
units.Acts 19:24: A silversmith named Demetrius, who made silver shrines of Artemis, provided considerable business for the craftsmen.
units.Acts 19:25: He gathered them and the workers in related trades and said, “Men, you know that our prosperity comes from this business.
units.Acts 19:26: You see and hear that not only in Ephesus but in almost all Asia this Paul has persuaded and turned away a considerable crowd, saying that things made by hands are not gods.
units.Acts 19:27: There is danger not only that this trade of ours will fall into disrepute, but also that the temple of the great goddess Artemis will be reckoned as nothing, and that she whom all Asia and the inhabited world worship will be stripped of her magnificence.”
units.Acts 19:28: When they heard this, they became full of rage and cried out, “Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!”
units.Acts 19:29: The city was filled with confusion. They rushed together into the theater, seizing Gaius and Aristarchus, Macedonians who traveled with Paul.
units.1 Kings 17:1: Elijah the prophet, the Tishbite from Thesbon in Gilead, said to Ahab, “As the Lord, the God of hosts, the God of Israel, lives, before whom I stand, there will be neither dew nor rain these years except through the utterance of my word.”
units.1 Kings 17:2: The Lord’s word came to Elijah:
units.1 Kings 17:3: “Go from here eastward and hide yourself at the Chorrath wadi, which faces the Jordan.
units.1 Kings 17:4: You will drink water from the wadi, and I will command the ravens to sustain you there.”
units.1 Kings 17:5: Elijah acted according to the Lord’s word and stayed at the Chorrath wadi facing the Jordan.
units.1 Kings 17:6: The ravens brought him bread in the morning and meat in the evening, and he drank water from the wadi.
units.1 Kings 19:1: Ahab reported to Jezebel his wife all that Elijah had done, and how he had killed the prophets with the sword.
units.1 Kings 19:2: Jezebel sent to Elijah and said, “If you are Elijah, I am Jezebel! May the god do thus to me and add more, for at this time tomorrow I will make your life like the life of one of them!”
units.1 Kings 19:3: Elijah was afraid, rose, and went for his life. He came to Beer-sheba in Judah and left his young attendant there.
units.1 Kings 19:4: He himself went a day’s journey into the wilderness, came, and sat under a single broom bush. He asked that his life might end and said, “Let it be enough now! I pray Thee, take my life from me, Lord, for I am no better than my fathers.”
units.1 Kings 19:5: He lay down and slept there under a plant. Behold, someone touched him and said to him, “Rise and eat.”
units.1 Kings 19:6: Elijah looked, and there at his head were a hearth cake of spelt and a flask of water. He rose, ate, and drank, then lay down again.
units.1 Kings 19:7: The Lord’s angel returned a second time, touched him, and said to him, “Rise, eat, for the journey is too much for you.”
units.1 Kings 19:8: He rose, ate, and drank, and went in the strength of that food forty days and forty nights to Mount Horeb.
units.Ezekiel 8:1: In the sixth year, in the fifth month, on the fifth of the month, I was sitting in the house, and Judah’s elders were sitting before me. The Lord’s hand came upon me,
units.Ezekiel 8:2: and I saw, and behold, the likeness of a man: from His waist downward, fire, and from His waist upward, like the appearance of electrum.
units.Ezekiel 8:3: He stretched out the likeness of a hand and lifted me by the crown of my head. A spirit lifted me between earth and heaven and brought me to Jerusalem in a vision of God, to the entrance of the inner gate facing north, where the pillar of the one acquiring stood.
units.Ezekiel 8:4: And behold, the glory of the Lord God of Israel was there, in accordance with the vision I had seen in the plain.
units.Acts 8:26: An angel of the Lord spoke to Philip, saying, “Rise and go south to the road that descends from Jerusalem to Gaza.” This is a desert road.
units.Acts 8:27: He rose and went. And look—an Ethiopian man, a eunuch and an official of Candace, queen of the Ethiopians, who was over all her treasury, had come to Jerusalem to worship.
units.Acts 8:28: He was returning, seated in his chariot, and reading the prophet Isaiah.
units.Acts 8:29: The Spirit said to Philip, “Go near and join this chariot.”
units.Acts 8:30: Philip ran up, heard him reading Isaiah the prophet, and said, “Do you understand what you are reading?”
units.Acts 8:31: He said, “How could I, unless someone guides me?” And he invited Philip to come up and sit with him.
units.Acts 8:32: The passage of Scripture he was reading was this: “Like a sheep He was led to slaughter, and as a lamb is silent before its shearer, so He does not open His mouth.
units.Acts 8:33: In His humiliation His judgment was taken away. Who will recount His generation? For His life is taken from the earth.”
units.Acts 8:34: The eunuch said to Philip, “I ask you, about whom does the prophet say this—about himself or about someone else?”
units.Acts 8:35: Philip opened his mouth and, beginning from this Scripture, proclaimed to him the good news of Jesus.
units.Acts 8:36: As they went along the road, they came to some water, and the eunuch said, “Look, water! What prevents me from being baptized?”
units.Acts 8:38: He ordered the chariot to stop. Both Philip and the eunuch went down into the water, and Philip baptized him.
units.Acts 8:39: When they came up out of the water, the Spirit of the Lord snatched Philip away, and the eunuch saw him no more, for he went on his way rejoicing.
units.Acts 8:40: Philip was found at Azotus, and as he passed through, he proclaimed the good news in all the towns until he came to Caesarea.
units.Psalms 144:18: The Lord is near to all who call on Him, to all who call on Him in truth.
units.Psalms 144:19: He will fulfill the will of those who fear Him; He will hear their plea and save them.
units.Psalms 144:20: The Lord guards all who love Him, and all sinners He will utterly destroy.
units.Psalms 144:21: My mouth will speak the Lord’s praise, and let all flesh bless His holy name for the age and for the age of the age.
units.Deuteronomy 4:32: Ask now of the former days that were before you, from the day when God created man upon the earth, and from one end of heaven unto the other: has there been anything like this great matter, or has such a thing been heard?
units.Deuteronomy 4:33: Has a nation heard the voice of the living God speaking out of the midst of the fire, as you have heard, and lived?
units.Deuteronomy 4:34: Or has God attempted to go and take unto Himself a nation from the midst of a nation, by trial, and by signs, and by wonders, and by war, and by a mighty hand, and by an uplifted arm, and by great visions, according to all that the Lord our God did in Egypt before your eyes?
units.Deuteronomy 4:35: That you might know that the Lord your God, He is God, and there is none beside Him.
units.Deuteronomy 4:36: Out of heaven His voice was made heard, to instruct you; and upon earth He showed you His great fire, and you heard His words out of the midst of the fire.
units.Deuteronomy 4:37: Because He loved your fathers, He chose their seed after them, even you, and Himself brought you forth out of Egypt by His great strength,
units.Deuteronomy 4:38: to destroy nations great and mightier than you from before you, to bring you in, and to give you their land to inherit, as you have this day.
units.Deuteronomy 4:39: And you shall know this day, and lay it to mind, that the Lord your God, He is God in heaven above and upon earth beneath; there is none beside Him.
units.Deuteronomy 4:40: And you shall keep His ordinances and His commandments which I command you this day, that it may be well with you and with your sons after you, and that you may prolong your days upon the land which the Lord your God gives you for ever.
units.Ruth 2:8: Boaz said to Ruth, “Have you not heard, daughter? Do not go to glean in another field, and do not leave this one. Stay close here to my maidens.
units.Ruth 2:9: Keep your eyes on the field where they reap, and follow them. Behold, I have commanded the servants not to touch you. Whenever you are thirsty, go to the vessels and drink from where the servants draw water.”
units.Ruth 2:10: She fell on her face and bowed to the ground, and said to him, “Why have I found favour in your eyes, that you take notice of me, a foreign woman?”
units.Ruth 2:11: Boaz answered her, “I have been fully told all that you have done for your mother-in-law since your husband's death: how you left your father and mother and the land of your birth, and came to a people you had not known before.
units.Ruth 2:12: May the Lord repay your work, and may your reward be full from the Lord, the God of Israel, under whose wings you have come to trust.
units.Ruth 2:13: She said, “May I find favour in your eyes, my lord, for you have comforted me and spoken to the heart of your handmaid. And behold, I shall be as one of your maidservants.”
units.Ruth 2:14: Boaz said to her, “It is time to eat now. Come here, eat some bread, and dip your morsel in the vinegar.” Ruth sat beside the reapers, and Boaz heaped barley meal for her. She ate and was filled, and left some over.
units.Ruth 2:15: She arose to glean, and Boaz commanded his servants, “Let her glean even among the sheaves, and do not put her to shame.
units.Ruth 2:16: Be sure to carry some for her, and be sure to cast some for her from the heaped-up grain. Leave it, and she shall glean, and you shall not rebuke her.”
units.Acts 6:8: Stephen, full of grace and power, was doing great wonders and signs among the people.
units.Acts 6:9: But some from the synagogue called the Freedmen’s, including Cyrenians and Alexandrians and people from Cilicia and Asia, rose up and disputed with Stephen.
units.Acts 6:10: They could not withstand the wisdom and the Spirit with which he spoke.
units.Acts 6:11: Then they secretly persuaded men to say, “We have heard him speaking blasphemous words against Moses and God.”
units.Acts 6:12: They stirred up the people, the elders, and the scribes, and came upon him, seized him, and brought him to the council.
units.Acts 6:13: They set up false witnesses who said, “This man never stops speaking words against this holy place and the law.
units.Acts 6:14: For we have heard him say that this Jesus the Nazarene will destroy this place and change the customs Moses handed down to us.”
units.Acts 6:15: All who were seated in the council looked intently at him and saw his face like the face of an angel.
units.Romans 1:1: Paul, a slave of Christ Jesus, called as an apostle, set apart for the gospel of God,
units.Romans 1:2: which He promised beforehand through His prophets in holy Scriptures,
units.Romans 1:3: concerning His Son, who came from David’s seed according to the flesh,
units.Romans 1:4: who was designated Son of God in power according to the Spirit of holiness by resurrection from the dead, Jesus Christ our Lord,
units.Romans 1:5: through whom we received grace and apostleship for the obedience of faith among all the nations for His name,
units.Romans 1:6: among whom you also are, called by Jesus Christ:
units.Romans 1:7: to all who are in Rome, beloved of God, called as saints: grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
